fixed_statement:
Let \(\pi\in\AUT(\mathcal A)\), let \(\bar d=\pi(\bar c)\), let \(\mathcal A^*=(\mathcal A,\bar c,\bar d)\), and let \(R=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb N^2:\pi(x)=y\}\).
Assume \(R\) is definable in \(\mathcal A^*\) by a countable disjunction of parameter-free existential formulas.
\(\pi\) is \(\Sigma^{in}_1\)-definable in \(\mathcal A\) relative to the parameters \(\bar c\cup\pi(\bar c)\).
fixed_proof: By Lemma 7.2, \(\pi\) is \(\Sigma^{in}_1\)-definable in \(\mathcal A\) relative to \(\bar c\cup\bar d\). By Proposition 4, \(\bar d=\pi(\bar c)\), and the same \(\pi\) was chosen not to be \(\Sigma^{in}_1\)-definable in \(\mathcal A\) relative to \(\bar c\cup\pi(\bar c)\). This contradicts the choice of \(\pi\) in Proposition 4.
